structured.name: Ecuador
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: Straddling the equator on South America's Pacific coast between Colombia and Peru, Ecuador packs a coastal plain, high Andean sierra, and Amazonian jungle into a single small country. Cotopaxi, one of its Andean peaks, is the highest active volcano in the world. Petroleum, fish, timber and hydropower underpin an economy that also ships out crude oil, shellfish, bananas, fish, and gold.
prose.physicalGeography: Ecuador's territory divides into three distinct bands: a coastal plain known as the costa, an inter-Andean central highland region called the sierra, and a flat to rolling eastern jungle known as the oriente. The country sits on South America's Pacific coast, on the equator, between Colombia and Peru.
prose.climate: Conditions run tropical along the coast, cooling with elevation inland, and tropical again in the Amazonian jungle lowlands. Volcanic activity is concentrated along the Andes, where Sangay, at 5,230 meters, is mainland Ecuador's most active volcano, alongside others including Cotopaxi, Antisana, Cayambe, and Tungurahua. The Galapagos Islands have their own volcanoes, with the shield volcano Fernandina the most active among them. The country also faces frequent earthquakes, landslides, floods, and periodic droughts.
prose.economy: Ecuador runs a highly informal economy and uses the US dollar as its currency. It is a major banana exporter, with crude petroleum, shellfish, fish, and gold also among its top exports, and its industries span petroleum, food processing, textiles, wood products, and chemicals. The economy was hit hard by COVID-19 and remains fragile due to dependence on oil, though it has carried out successful debt restructuring while China has helped fund budget deficits.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Most Ecuadorians identify as Mestizo, of mixed Indigenous and White heritage, with smaller Montubio, Indigenous, White, Afroecuadorian, Mulatto, and Black populations. Roman Catholicism is the majority religion, followed by a substantial Protestant community that is mostly Evangelical, with smaller numbers of Adventists, Jehovah's Witnesses, and those with no religious affiliation.
